title: BMAL1 downregulation exacerbates age-related nonalcoholic steatohepatitis by promoting NLRP3 inflammasome activation via HIF-1a-mediated glycolysis.
authors: Ren, Yujie; Lv, Dongying; Chen, Jiayan; Chen, Wenjing; Chen, Chu; Zhang, Lizong; Tu, Jue; Zhu, Keyan; Wang, Dejun; Cai, Zhaowei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究BMAL1通过HIF-1α调控糖酵解与NLRP3炎症小体在衰老相关脂肪性肝炎中的作用，核心为代谢与炎症通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Epidemiological studies have demonstrated higher incidence and mortality rate of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) in the elderly population than in younger groups. However, the mechanisms underlying this age-related exacerbation remain poorly understood. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to elucidate the specific pathways through which aging exacerbates NASH progression, using an integrated in vivo and in vitro model. METHODS: Aged (18-month-old) and young (6-week-old) mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) for 16 weeks to induce NASH. A senescence-associated cellular model of NASH was established by co-treating murine hepatocyte AML-12 with H(2)O(2) and free fatty acid (FFA). Gene expression profiling of liver tissue was performed using RNA sequencing to identify molecular signatures. Interventions were as follows: (1) In vitro, BMAL1 overexpression plasmids were transfected into AML-12 cells, followed by treatment with 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG, a glycolysis inhibitor) and 2-methoxyestradiol (2-ME2, a HIF-1alpha inhibitor); (2) in vivo, hepatocyte-specific BMAL1 overexpression was achieved in aged HFD-fed mice through adeno-associated virus serotype 8 (AAV8) delivery. Mechanism validation was performed using biochemical assays, Western blot, cell staining, molecular docking, and Co-IP. RESULTS: Aged HFD-fed mice exhibited more severe NASH phenotypes than young mice. Transcriptomic analysis identified NLRP3-related signaling and circadian rhythm pathways as central contributors to age-specific NASH pathogenesis. These mice also exhibited elevated NLRP3 inflammasome activity, enhanced glycolysis, and reduced BMAL1 expression. In senescent NASH cells, BMAL1 overexpression along with 2-DG or 2-ME2 treatment significantly downregulated NLRP3 expression and attenuated lipid accumulation, inflammation, oxidative stress, and fibrosis. Mechanistically, BMAL1 directly bound to HIF-1alpha, thereby suppressing glycolysis. Hepatocyte-specific BMAL1 overexpression in aged HFD-fed mice markedly inhibited glycolysis and NLRP3 activation, resulting in an improvement in NASH-related pathologies. CONCLUSION: This study revealed a novel mechanism in which BMAL1 downregulation under aging and HFD conditions promotes NASH progression by binding to HIF-1alpha and modulating the glycolysis-NLRP3 inflammasome axis.
abstract_zh: 引言：流行病学研究显示，非酒精性脂肪性肝炎（NASH）在老年人群中的发病率和死亡率高于年轻群体。然而，年龄相关加重的潜在机制仍知之甚少。目的：本研究旨在利用整合的体内和体外模型，阐明衰老加剧NASH进展的具体通路。方法：将老年（18月龄）和年轻（6周龄）小鼠喂食高脂饮食（HFD）16周以诱导NASH。通过将小鼠肝细胞AML-12与H(2)O(2)和游离脂肪酸（FFA）共处理，建立NASH的衰老相关细胞模型。使用RNA测序对肝组织进行基因表达谱分析，以识别分子特征。干预措施如下：（1）体外，将BMAL1过表达质粒转染至AML-12细胞，随后用2-脱氧-D-葡萄糖（2-DG，一种糖酵解抑制剂）和2-甲氧基雌二醇（2-ME2，一种HIF-1α抑制剂）处理；（2）体内，通过腺相关病毒血清型8（AAV8）递送，在老年HFD喂养小鼠中实现肝细胞特异性BMAL1过表达。机制验证采用生化检测、Western blot、细胞染色、分子对接和Co-IP进行。结果：老年HFD喂养小鼠表现出比年轻小鼠更严重的NASH表型。转录组分析将NLRP3相关信号和昼夜节律通路识别为年龄特异性NASH发病机制的核心贡献因素。这些小鼠还表现出NLRP3炎症小体活性升高、糖酵解增强和BMAL1表达降低。在衰老NASH细胞中，BMAL1过表达联合2-DG或2-ME2处理显著下调NLRP3表达，并减轻脂质积累、炎症、氧化应激和纤维化。机制上，BMAL1直接结合HIF-1α，从而抑制糖酵解。老年HFD喂养小鼠中肝细胞特异性BMAL1过表达显著抑制糖酵解和NLRP3激活，导致NASH相关病理改善。结论：本研究揭示了一种新机制，其中衰老和HFD条件下BMAL1下调通过结合HIF-1α并调节糖酵解-NLRP3炎症小体轴，促进NASH进展。
